posts.text: A peregrine falcon dives at over 240 mph. Tiny bony baffles in its nostrils are the only reason the air pressure does not wreck its lungs.
comments: Fastest animal on earth, and the engineering that makes it survivable is in the nose.

posts.text: Baby green iguanas cost $20 to $100. That low starting price is exactly why so many owners underestimate what they are taking on.
comments: Color morphs are a different market entirely. Albino, hypomelanistic, axanthic, and purple translucent lines commonly run $300 to $1,000 or more.
The real cost is the adult enclosure. It has to be custom-built or walk-in, because no commercial tank is large enough, and that is before the lighting cluster goes in.
Then there is the vet. Iguana-specific problems like metabolic bone disease treatment or egg-binding surgery run into real money, and emergency care for this species is not cheap.
If someone you know is eyeing a $30 baby iguana, this is the page → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/green-iguana-cost-guide/

posts.text: In some anglerfish species the male fuses permanently to the female. Skin and blood vessels merge until he is little more than a built-in supply of sperm.
comments: He is a fraction of her size to start with. The deep sea does not do romance. Card is here if you want the rest → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-ultimate-clingy-partner/

posts.text: A wandering albatross has a tendon that locks its wings open, so it glides for hours over open ocean without a single flap.
comments: Wingspan up to 11 feet, the largest of any living bird.

posts.text: Red-eared sliders are sold cheap and small, which is what makes their real cost so easy to underestimate. The animal is genuinely inexpensive. What it grows into is not.
comments: Hatchlings run $10 to $40, with most listings clustering at $15 to $30. Adults go $40 to $100 or more depending on size and condition.
The single biggest line item is a 100-plus gallon enclosure. That is the number nobody quotes at the pet store counter.
Federal law restricts the sale of turtles under 4 inches, not ownership of them. Those are two different things and the distinction matters.
Full cost picture before the tank upgrade sneaks up on you → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/red-eared-slider-cost-guide/

posts.text: An owl's eyes are not balls. They are fixed tubes locked into the skull, so it rotates the whole head up to 270 degrees instead.
comments: Incredible night vision, at the price of never once glancing sideways.

posts.text: A giant squid's eye runs up to 27 cm across, roughly a dinner plate, built to catch the faintest bioluminescent flicker in the deep.
comments: Largest eyes in the animal kingdom, aimed at almost total darkness. Full card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/dinner-plate-eyes/

posts.text: Almost every common betta illness traces back to one of two things: water quality or water temperature. That is genuinely good news, because it means the first move is always the same.
comments: Fin rot shows as frayed, ragged, or discolored fins. Mild cases respond to clean water and aquarium salt, with antibiotics if it is further along.
Velvet is the one that moves fast. A fine gold or rust colored dusty sheen, caused by Oodinium, and it can be fatal quickly, so early treatment matters.
Columnaris is bacterial and highly contagious between fish, which matters a lot if you run more than one tank.
Worth having open before you need it rather than during → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/betta-fish-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Reindeer eyes shift from golden in summer to deep blue in winter. They are the only mammals known to change eye color with the season.
comments: The winter version pulls in more light during Arctic twilight.

posts.text: A common swift can stay airborne for up to 10 months. It eats, sleeps, and mates in the air, and only lands to breed.
comments: Ten months without touching down. Worth remembering next time a flight feels long.

posts.text: Wet tail is the one condition every hamster owner needs to recognize on sight. It can be fatal within 24 to 48 hours without treatment.
comments: A large veterinary study on causes of death in pet hamsters found it in roughly 7 to 8 percent of the animals studied, both the most commonly diagnosed condition and the leading specific cause of death.
It is typically triggered by stress, transport, overcrowding, poor hygiene, or a sudden diet change. Do not wait to see if it improves, that is a same-day vet visit.
Overgrown teeth are the quieter one. Hamster teeth grow continuously, so watch for dropped food, drooling, and weight loss.
Short lifespan means everything moves fast in this species. Full list here → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/hamster-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Magpies were the first non-mammal to pass the mirror test. Put a colored dot on their feathers and they immediately try to get it off.
comments: A cleaner wrasse has since joined them on that list. Send this to whoever still says bird brain → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/magpie-self-awareness/

posts.text: A cuttlefish ripples hypnotic patterns across its skin at speed, and the light show freezes crabs in place just long enough to strike.
comments: Hunting by hypnosis, and that is the literal mechanism, not a metaphor.

posts.text: Ball pythons are hardy, and they are also sensitive to husbandry mistakes in specific, predictable ways. Most of what goes wrong is temperature, humidity, or hygiene.
comments: Respiratory infection is the signature one. Too-cold temperatures, wrong humidity, a dirty enclosure, or ongoing stress, and vets see a seasonal spike each winter as enclosures cool down.
That one needs prescription antibiotics, not a wait-and-see. Untreated it can progress to pneumonia and kill the snake.
Scale rot is the other regular. Discolored belly scales, blisters or sores, scales that feel soft, and a foul smell, all from damp dirty substrate.
Nearly all of this is preventable, which is the useful part → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/ball-python-health-issues-guide/

posts.text: Tardigrades survive boiling water, freezing, and the vacuum of space by shutting their metabolism almost entirely off.
comments: Half a millimeter long and harder to kill than anything you can actually see.

posts.text: Cheetahs purr continuously, even while exhaling. They are the only large cat that never truly roars.
comments: It is one or the other in big cats. Cheetahs took the purr. Card here → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/cant-stop-purring/

posts.text: The chinchilla is not the expensive part. The cage, the wheel, and keeping the room cold enough are where the budget actually goes.
comments: Most complete setups land between $455 and $1,225, depending mostly on cage quality and whether you adopt or buy from a breeder.
The line item nobody puts on the shopping list is air conditioning. Chinchillas overheat in a room that feels perfectly comfortable to a person, so summer becomes a recurring cost.
Bedding and chews are worth spending up on. Unscented paper bedding, and chews sturdy enough to actually last.
Send this to whoever is pricing one out right now → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/chinchilla-cost-guide/

posts.text: Pangolins are the only mammals covered in scales. Threatened, they curl into a tight ball and let the armor do the work.
comments: A mammal that went and grew what looks like armadillo plating.

posts.text: Box jellyfish have 24 eyes in four clusters and see in full color. They have no brain at all.
comments: The eyes are structurally similar to ours. There is simply nothing behind them to process the picture.

posts.text: Savannah monitors are cheap to buy, and that low price is part of a real problem with how this species gets marketed and cared for.
comments: Juveniles run $150 to $300, adults $300 to $800. Part of why they stay affordable is that many are wild-caught or farmed in bulk, which also means a share of them arrive stressed.
The enclosure dominates the cost. An adult needs an 8x4x4 foot custom build, and commercial tanks do not go there.

Many pet savannah monitors die in their early teens or younger, well short of the 15 to 20 years good husbandry supports, from fatty liver disease, kidney failure, or gout, nearly all tied to overfeeding.
The full picture, before the cheap price tag does its work → https://beastlyfacts.com/blog/savannah-monitor-cost-guide/

posts.text: Leafcutter ants do not eat the leaves they carry. They feed them to a fungus farmed underground, and the fungus is the actual food.
comments: They have been running agriculture for over 50 million years.
